- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior day), true outcome often corrects downward within 3–7 days; apply downward bias of 3–8% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently below recent 5-day average, true outcome often reverses upward; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.10+), model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of smoothing or delay in forecast adjustment.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early days (1–7) and underestimates in late days (24–30); apply asymmetric correction: +2% for first 7 days, -2% for last 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows strong recent positive sentiment, model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days to align with mean.
